pods.domain: Monorepo tooling, CI, Docker Compose, shared libraries and configuration

stories.title: Monorepo setup with Nx and pnpm workspaces

acceptanceCriteria.text: pnpm-workspace.yaml defines apps/, services/, and packages/ as workspace packages
Nx workspace is configured with a project graph covering every app, service, and package
Every project (apps, services, packages) defines Nx targets for lint, typecheck, test, and build; frontends also define serve and packages/ui also defines storybook
Nx tags enforce module boundaries so an app can depend on packages/* but never on another app
A single `docker compose up` starts shell, mfe-auth, mfe-chat, mfe-settings, auth-service, conversation-service, Postgres, and Ollama
Docker Compose also starts Prometheus and Grafana pre-wired to scrape the services
A .env.example file lists every environment variable needed by every service, with safe local defaults
packages/shared-types defines the API contracts and DTOs consumed by both frontends and services
packages/eslint-config provides a flat ESLint config with typescript-eslint used by every project
packages/tsconfig provides shared tsconfig bases used by every project, with `tsc --noEmit` passing on each
Every project's feature folders only import from shared/ and from other features' index.ts, never from feature internals
CI runs `nx affected` for lint, typecheck, test, and build on every pull request
CI fails the build if any project reports a lint or typecheck error
Nx task results are cached in CI to avoid re-running unaffected projects

pods.domain: Shared UI component library and design tokens (packages/ui)

stories.title: Core component library on shadcn/ui + Base UI

acceptanceCriteria.text: packages/ui implements Button, Input, Textarea, Label, Form field, Card, Dialog, Dropdown menu, Select, Tabs, Toast, Badge, Avatar, Skeleton, Tooltip, and typography components on shadcn/ui using Base UI primitives (not Radix)
Components are themed with Tailwind design tokens for color, spacing, radius, and typography, and support both light and dark mode
Typography components and scale follow the shadcn Typeset
Every microfrontend (mfe-auth, mfe-chat, mfe-settings) uses only design-system components for UI primitives, with no ad-hoc primitive markup
Every component in packages/ui has Storybook stories covering its variants and states
The Storybook accessibility (Axe) addon is enabled and reports zero violations for every story
The `storybook` Nx target builds and serves the design system's Storybook instance

pods.domain: Host application: layout, routing, module federation, auth guard, resilience

stories.title: Host app with Module Federation and routing

acceptanceCriteria.text: The shell app is a Vite Module Federation host that lazy-loads mfe-auth, mfe-chat, and mfe-settings as remotes at runtime
Top-level TanStack Router routes are type-safe and file-based, defined in the shell
React, React DOM, TanStack Router, TanStack Query, and the design system are shared as singletons across host and remotes
The shell exposes a shared TanStack Query client used by all remotes
Unauthenticated users navigating to any chat or configuration route are redirected to the login route (FR3)
If a remote (mfe-auth, mfe-chat, or mfe-settings) fails to load, the shell renders a scoped error state for that area only
The rest of the application (navigation, other loaded domains) continues to work when one remote fails
A test simulating a remote load failure verifies the shell degrades gracefully without a full-app crash

pods.domain: Authentication: registration, login, logout, session/token validation

acceptanceCriteria.text: Registration form collects email and password, validated on client and server
A duplicate email is rejected with a validation error and no account is created
An invalid password (not meeting the policy) is rejected with a validation error
Passwords are stored hashed in Postgres via Prisma; plaintext passwords are never persisted or logged
After successful registration the user can immediately log in with those credentials
Valid credentials log the user in and land them on their chat list
Invalid credentials show one generic error message that does not reveal which field was wrong
Auth tokens are issued as httpOnly cookies, not accessible to client-side JavaScript
Logout invalidates the session so subsequent authenticated requests are rejected

stories.title: Session validation on every protected request (FR3)

acceptanceCriteria.text: conversation-service validates the caller's token on every request and rejects missing/invalid tokens with 401
auth-service issues and validates tokens used by other services
The shell redirects the user to login when the frontend detects an expired or invalid session

pods.domain: Chats, streaming messaging, queueing, attachments, and LLM provider adapters

stories.title: Chat CRUD and history persistence (FR4, FR8)

acceptanceCriteria.text: A user can create, list, rename, open, and delete chats
Chat history (messages) persists in Postgres and is restored after a page reload or a new login
Deleting a chat removes it and its messages so they no longer appear or load
Every chat read, update, delete, and stream request is checked server-side against the authenticated user's ownership
User B requesting user A's chat ID (get, update, delete, or stream) receives 403 or 404
Chat list and search endpoints never return another user's chats

stories.title: Provider and model selection per chat (FR6)

acceptanceCriteria.text: The user chooses an LLM provider (Ollama, OpenAI, or Anthropic) and a model when creating or editing a chat
The selected provider and model are persisted per chat
All subsequent messages in that chat use the persisted provider and model

stories.title: Send message and streamed response (FR9, FR10, FR12, UC3)

acceptanceCriteria.text: A sent text message is persisted immediately and shown in the chat
The LLM response streams token by token (via SSE) and renders incrementally in the UI
The full conversation history of the chat is sent to the LLM as context on every request
The user can stop a response mid-stream, and the partial response is saved to history
The completed response is saved and reappears after a reload
Messages sent while a chat is waiting for or streaming a response are added to that chat's FIFO queue
Queued messages are shown in a distinct 'queued' UI state
The user can edit or cancel a queued message before its processing starts
Queued messages are processed one at a time, in order, after the current response finishes
A user can have multiple chats generating responses at the same time
Switching between chats does not interrupt or lose any in-progress stream
The UI stays responsive with at least 5 chats streaming simultaneously
A single common adapter interface is implemented for Ollama, OpenAI, and Anthropic
conversation-service selects the adapter implementation based on the chat's configured provider
Adding a new provider requires changes only inside the adapter layer, with no changes to controllers, queue, or other domains

stories.title: File attachment upload and validation (FR13, FR14, FR15, UC5)

acceptanceCriteria.text: A user can attach one or more files to a message
Only .txt, .pdf, .png, and .jpeg/.jpg files are accepted; both file extension and MIME type are validated on the client and on the server
Files over 10 MB or of a disallowed type are rejected before upload with a clear, specific error message
Text and PDF attachment content is extracted as text and included in the LLM request context
Image attachments (.png/.jpeg) are sent as image input for models that support vision
If the selected model cannot handle an attached file's type, the user is shown a clear message before or instead of sending

stories.title: Provider error handling and retry (Reliability NFR)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Provider errors, timeouts, and rate limits are caught and surfaced to the user without crashing the chat
The user can retry a message that failed due to a provider error
A failed queued message is skipped/marked failed without blocking the rest of the queue from processing

pods.domain: Configuration microfrontend for browser-only LLM API key management

acceptanceCriteria.text: The configuration page in mfe-settings is reachable from the app navigation
The user can enter, update, and remove an API key for each provider that needs one (OpenAI, Anthropic)
Ollama is shown as not requiring a key
API keys are stored only in the browser (e.g. localStorage), scoped to the logged-in user
API keys are never sent to or stored in the database, on disk, or in server logs
Logging in as a different user does not expose a previously logged-in user's stored keys
The browser sends the relevant provider's API key with each request that calls that provider's LLM (e.g. a request header)
conversation-service uses the key only for that single request and does not persist it
The key is redacted from any logs or error responses produced by conversation-service

stories.title: Masked display, test connection, and missing-key messaging (FR20, UC8)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Saved keys are displayed masked (for example, sk-...a1b2), never in full
A 'Test connection' action validates the key against the provider and shows success or a clear failure reason
Sending a message to a provider with no configured key shows a clear message in the chat with a link to the configuration page
Removing a saved key causes that provider's chats to prompt for a key again on the next message

pods.domain: Logging, metrics/dashboards, and the cross-cutting test suite

acceptanceCriteria.text: Every request to auth-service and conversation-service is tagged with a correlation ID, generated or propagated from the caller
Logs are structured (JSON) and include the correlation ID on every log line for that request
API keys, passwords, and tokens are redacted from all log output
Prometheus scrapes request rate, latency, error rate, and active-stream metrics from auth-service and conversation-service
Grafana ships with a preconfigured dashboard visualizing these metrics
Prometheus and Grafana start automatically as part of `docker compose up`

stories.title: Testing strategy: unit, contract, and performance tests

acceptanceCriteria.text: Vitest unit tests cover business logic and each LLM provider adapter with the LLMs mocked
Pact contract tests verify the API contracts between frontends and services
A K6 test validates first-token latency is about 1 second and the system stays responsive with at least 5 concurrent streaming chats
Coverage targets are documented and enforced as part of the CI pipeline
Playwright end-to-end tests cover UC1 through UC8 against the docker-compose environment
Axe accessibility checks run as part of the e2e or Storybook CI pipeline with no critical violations
The e2e suite runs in CI and its results gate merges
